items.definition:
free (as in freedom, not cost)
The project promotes libre software, emphasizing user freedom.

lacking in quantity or quality; meager
They survived on a meager diet during the famine.

Small or meager.
He received a paltry sum for his hard work.

Having developed certain abilities or proclivities at an earlier age than usual.
The precocious child started reading at the age of three.

(Of a person or their behavior) failing to observe the limits of what is permitted or appropriate.
It would be presumptuous of me to assume I know what you're thinking.

resembling or characteristic of a hallucinatory experience
The movie had some really trippy visual effects.

uncontrolled; unconstrained
His unbridled enthusiasm was infectious.

Deliberate and unprovoked; sexually immodest.
The wanton destruction of property was condemned by the community.

Using or expressing dry, especially mocking, humor; slightly distorted.
He gave a wry smile, acknowledging the irony of the situation.

Causing moral revulsion; very bad.
The weather was abominable, with heavy rain and strong winds.

Relating to Aramaic, a Semitic language.
Some parts of the Bible were originally written in Aramaic.

relating to or consisting of chromosomes
Genetic disorders can be caused by chromosomal abnormalities.

making use of a situation or treating others unfairly in order to benefit from their work
The company was criticized for its exploitative labor practices.

relating to ancient Greek history, culture, or art
The museum displayed many Hellenic artifacts.

relating to Greek history, language, and culture from the death of Alexander the Great to the defeat of Cleopatra and Mark Antony
The Hellenistic period saw the spread of Greek culture across the Mediterranean.

believing in or practicing religious heresy
His views were considered heretical by the church authorities.

too large, extensive, or extreme to measure
The impact of her work was immeasurable.

unchanging over time or unable to be changed
The laws of physics are considered immutable.

unable to be challenged or denied
The evidence was indisputable, proving his guilt.

Relating to the science of metallurgy
The company specializes in metallurgical engineering.

Having unlimited power
Many religions believe in an omnipotent God.

relating to or involving reconstruction, especially of damaged tissue
She underwent reconstructive surgery after the accident.

characterized by retaliation; striking back
The country threatened retaliatory measures if the sanctions were imposed.

not belonging to or recognized by any country as a citizen
Many refugees become stateless individuals.

bad-tempered and unfriendly
The surly waiter ignored our requests.

Not tied or restricted.
The wild horse ran unbound across the plains.

Causing one to lose courage or confidence.
The silence in the old house was unnerving.

Of great importance or influence.
The committee had to make a weighty decision.

Involving conflict or opposition.
The two teams had an adversarial relationship.

occurring or existing before a particular war, especially the American Civil War
The antebellum architecture of the South is quite distinctive.

sacrilegious against God or sacred things; profane
His comments were considered blasphemous by many religious leaders.

attractive or beautiful (chiefly Scottish and northern English)
The bonny lass had a lovely smile.

existing or occurring in the same period of time
The two events were contemporaneous, happening at roughly the same time.

capable of erection
Erectile dysfunction is a common medical condition.

relating to an imaginary or spiritual world; ethereal
The ancient ruins had an otherworldly beauty that captivated visitors.

relating to or expressed in terms of a parameter or parameters
The study used a parametric statistical test to analyze the data.

relating to a reflex; referring back to the subject
Sneezing is a reflexive action.

below the threshold of conscious perception
Some advertisements use subliminal messages to influence consumers.

in bed
He lay abed, unable to sleep.

pessimistic about the market; resembling a bear
Investors are feeling bearish about the economy's prospects.

belonging to an earlier time
They reminisced about bygone days and old friends.

proportionate; corresponding in size or degree
His salary is commensurate with his experience and responsibilities.

convenient and practical, although possibly improper or immoral
It was more expedient to take the shortcut, even though it was muddy.

pitifully sad and abandoned or lonely
The stray dog looked forlorn in the rain.

consisting of small parts that are disconnected or incomplete
The police only had fragmentary evidence to go on.

extravagantly bright or showy, typically tasteless
She wore a gaudy necklace with too many jewels.

relating to homeopathy, a system of alternative medicine
She prefers homeopathic remedies for her allergies.

unable to be defended or justified
His actions were completely indefensible.

unable to be divided or separated
The nation declared itself to be one and indivisible.

not producing any or the desired effect
His efforts to organize the event were ineffectual.

relating to oceanography
The research vessel conducted extensive oceanographic surveys.

exaggerated or excessive
The media's reaction to the incident was completely overblown.

affecting the mind or behavior
Cannabis is a psychoactive substance.

relating to or found in sacred writings or scriptures
The sermon included many scriptural references.

situated or applied under the skin
The medication is administered by subcutaneous injection.

excessively willing to obey others
She was subservient to her parents' wishes.

Having knowledge or being aware of.
He was cognizant of the risks involved in the venture.

relating to or influenced by Sigmund Freud and his methods of psychoanalysis
He made a Freudian slip and revealed his true feelings.

Not able to be forgotten or removed.
The experience left an indelible mark on her memory.

Between planets.
Scientists are planning future interplanetary missions to Mars.

Showing a lack of respect for people or things that are generally taken seriously.
His irreverent comments often shocked the more traditional members of the audience.

Traveling from place to place.
The itinerant preacher traveled from town to town, spreading his message.

Relating to lymph or the lymphatic system
The lymphatic system is crucial for immune function.

Easily shaped; adaptable
Gold is a highly malleable metal.
